items.briefing:
South Australia has launched a Royal Commission into artificial intelligence, signalling growing government scrutiny of AI use across Australia — something staff at registered training organisations should be aware of as AI tools become more common in education. Separately, privacy advocates are urging Australia to ban smart glasses capable of covert filming, raising concerns about consent and surveillance in shared spaces like classrooms and training facilities.

An Australian startup, Quantum Lock, has developed new technology using quantum physics to detect cyberattacks on embedded devices, reflecting local innovation in cybersecurity.

**Practical tip:** If you see someone wearing smart glasses in your workplace or training rooms, check your organisation's recording consent policy and report any concerns to your manager.

featured.title: South Australia launches Royal Commission into artificial intelligence
featured.quote: Government-level AI oversight signals Australia's commitment to regulating emerging technology risks.
